subject: Data Engineering
title: HDFS: The Distributed File System
description: A micro-lesson that makes HDFS: The Distributed File System usable.

hook.text: You can't process a petabyte on one disk. HDFS spreads data across thousands of machines.

buildup.text: HDFS splits files into 128 MB blocks and replicates each block across three machines for safety.

discovery.text: If a machine dies, HDFS automatically re-replicates the lost blocks from surviving copies.

twist.text: HDFS is optimized for large sequential reads. Small random reads — like database lookups — are slow.

climax.text: HDFS proved that cheap hardware plus smart software could replace expensive enterprise storage.

punchline.text: Cheap disks, smart replication. That's HDFS.

quiz.question: How does HDFS protect against hardware failure?
options: By replicating each data block across multiple machines
By backing up to tape drives
